# updating 9/23/26

# From the inital paper methods
Parent/caregivereadolescent dyads completed an online (Qualtrics, LCC, Provo, UT) cross-sectional questionnaire from November to December 2021 (92% of adults identified as a parent; hereafter, parents or caregivers will be referred to as parents). Researchers paid Qualtrics to recruit participants to complete questionnaires from a proprietary panelist database15 using nonprobabilistic sampling16 to include households with adolescents (11e14 years) and to enforce quota constraints regarding race and ethnicity to ensure a diverse sample (African American or Black, Asian, Hispanic or Latino, White or Caucasian, each at 24% of the sample, and Hawaiian or Pacific Islander and Native American at 2% each). Qualtrics panelists are recruited through diverse channels such as marketing through airline lists, social media platforms, and online shopping centers. To reach parentechild dyads, Qualtrics advertised recruitment materials, which included a link to an online screening questionnaire, to panelists who were parents. Screening questions at the beginning of the online questionnaire were used to determine whether respondents met inclusion criteria, including being comfortable reading English (parent and adolescent), eating meals or snacks at least once in a typical week when a main caregiver or other caregivers (defined as other parents or adult family members, but not teachers or school staff) were not around (adolescent), being the primary person responsible for providing food (parent), living with the adolescent 3 or more days per week (parent), and reporting household income as 185% of federal poverty income guidelines or lower (parent).17 Financial eligibility for the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children is determined by having an annual household income 185% or less of the federal poverty income guidelines.18 Qualtrics collected data until 622 responses were classified as “good completes,” meaning respondents completed the entire survey. Qualtrics then provided researchers with a Microsoft Excel file containing these data. Researchers also had access to all survey responses, including those who ended the survey early.

# Food related variables
```{r}
# this function will filter the dataframe based on the food name and create a list with 3 datasets. The first are all columns that include the name, the second is the ieo, and the third is general intake of the food

filter_food_rows <- function(df, food_name) {
  food_rows <- df %>% filter(grepl(food_name, description, ignore.case = FALSE))
  
  food_rows_ieo <- food_rows %>%
    filter(grepl("when your main caregiver was not around\\?", description, ignore.case = FALSE))
  
  food_rows_gen <- food_rows %>%
    filter(!grepl("when your main caregiver was not around\\?", description, ignore.case = FALSE))
  
  return(list(
    all = food_rows,
    ieo = food_rows_ieo,
    general = food_rows_gen
  ))
}

```

# all of the food groups
```{r}
allFOODS <- c("friedChicken", "processedMeat", "burgers", "fruitJuice", "wholeGrainBread", "cookedWholeGrains", "candyChocolate", "cookiesCakes", "frozenDeserts", "chips", 
"sugaryCereal", "cereal", "soda", "energyDrinks", "sportDrinks", "water", "milk", 
"fruit", "greenSalad", "fruitDrinks", "fries", "potatoes", "veggies", "beans", 
"pizza", "tacosBurritos", "heatServe")
```


```{r}
# Initialize an empty list that will store labels for each food item
allLabels <- list()

# Loop through each food item name contained in allFOODS
for (food in allFOODS) {
  # Check whether an object with this food name exists in the environment
  if (exists(food)) {
    # Retrieve the object and store it in food_data
    food_data <- get(food)
    # Check that the object contains an element called $all
    if (!is.null(food_data$all)) {
      # Extract the qual codes from the $all element
      quals <- food_data$all$qual
      # Extract the descriptions and convert them to character strings
      descs <- paste0(food_data$all$description)
      # Create a named vector where descriptions are values
      # and qual codes are the corresponding names
      allLabels[[food]] <- setNames(descs, quals)
    } else {
      # Display a warning if the object does not contain a $all element
      warning(paste("No $all element in", food))
    }
    
  } else {
    # Display a warning if the object does not exist
    warning(paste("Object", food, "does not exist"))
  }
}
# Collapse the list of named vectors into a single named vector
flatLabels <- unlist(allLabels)
# Remove any prefix before the final period in each name,
# leaving only the qual code as the name
names(flatLabels) <- sub(".*\\.", "", names(flatLabels))
# View the resulting named vector (currently commented out)
View(flatLabels)
```

```{r}
# Append the labels stored in flatLabels to the existing Labels vector
Labels <- c(Labels, flatLabels)
```


## Convert into daily intakes
https://cancercontrol.cancer.gov/sites/default/files/2020-06/flashe-data-users-guide.pdf

Table 1. FLASHE original responses and converted daily frequency values.
| Original Response                         | Converted Daily Frequency | Qualtrics                 |
|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------|
| Never,  | 0                         | 1                         |
| 1 to 3 times during the past 7 days       | 0.29                      | 2                         |
| 4 to 6 times during the past 7 days       | 0.71                      | 3                         |
| 1 time per day, | 1                         | 4                         |
| 2 times per day, | 2                         | 5                         |
| 3 or more times per day                   | 3                         | 6                         |

```{r}
convert_food_column <- function(df, column_name, string) {
  mapping <- c(
    `1` = 0,
    `2` = 0.29,
    `3` = 0.71,
    `4` = 1,
    `5` = 2,
    `6` = 3
  )
  new_name <- paste0(column_name, string) #take the input column name and append the string to it
  df[[new_name]] <- mapping[as.character(df[[column_name]])] # map the new values in the mapping list to the column with the original column name call it the new column name
  df
}
```



```{r}
#make new column for the ieo
add_ieo_sum <- function(df, col_names, prefix) {
  # new mapping for the food variables into daily intake value from factors
  mapping <- c(
    `1` = 0,
    `2` = 0.29,
    `3` = 0.71,
    `4` = 1,
    `5` = 2,
    `6` = 3
  )
  new_col_names_vector<-c()
  for (x in col_names){
    new_name <- paste0(x, "_ieo") #take the input column name and append the string to it
    df[[new_name]] <- mapping[as.character(df[[x]])] # map the new values in the mapping list to the column with the original column name call it the new column name
    new_col_names_vector <- c(new_col_names_vector, new_name)
  }
  # Create the new column name dynamically
  new_col_name <- paste0(prefix, "_ieo") ##take the input column name and append the string to it
  print(new_col_name)
  print(df[, new_col_names_vector])
  # Compute row sums and add to the data frame
  df[[new_col_name]] <- rowSums(df[, new_col_names_vector], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  return(df)
}
```



```{r}
# Loop through each food variable
for (food in food_vars) {
  print(food)
  # Get the original column names, getting the independent eating
  original_col_names <- get(food)$ieo$qual
  print(original_col_names)
  
  # Add "_ieo_" to each column name
 # daily_col_names <- paste0(original_col_names, "_dailyFreq")
 # print(daily_col_names)
  
  # Apply the function using the modified column names
  df <- add_ieo_sum(df, original_col_names, food)
}
```

#create groups

| Food Group | Items |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Junk Foods | candy/chocolate + cookies/cake + potato chips + fried potatoes + frozen desserts |
| Junk Foods (without frozen desserts) | candy/chocolate + cookies/cake + potato chips + fried potatoes | 
| SSB | soda + energy drinks + sweetened fruit drinks + sports drinks | 
| SSB (without energy drinks) | soda + sweetened fruit drinks + sports drinks | 
| Junk Foods + SSB | soda + energy drinks + sweetened fruit drinks + sports drinks + candy/chocolate + cookies/cake + potato chips + fried potatoes + frozen desserts | 
| Junk Foods + SSB (without frozen desserts or energy drinks) | soda + sweetened fruit drinks + sports drinks + candy/chocolate + cookies/cake + potato chips + fried potatoes | 
| Sugary Foods | frozen dessert + cookies/cake + candy/chocolate + sugary cereal | 
| Fast/Convenience Foods | fried potatoes + fried chicken + pizza + tacos + burgers + heat and serve | 
| Fatty meat | fried chicken + burgers + processed meat | 
| Fruits and vegetables | 100% fruit juice + fruit + green salad + other non-fried vegetables + cooked beans + other potatoes | 
| All detrimental foods | pizza + heat and serve + tacos + fried chicken + burgers + processedmeat + fried potatoes + candy/chocolate + cookies/cake + potatochips + frozen desserts + sugary cereals + sweetened fruit drinks + soda + energy drinks + sports drinks |
| All beneficial foods | 100% fruit juice + water + fruit + green salad + other non-fried vegetables + cooked beans + whole grain bread + cooked whole grains + non-sugary cereal + other potatoes |

CGPQ Coercive control -> small = high coercion

```{r}
# Function to recode a column with custom values
recode_column <- function(df, column_name) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      !!paste0(column_name, "_rc") := recode(.data[[column_name]],
                                             `1` = 50L, 
                                             `2` = 40L, 
                                             `3` = 30L, 
                                             `4` = 20L, 
                                             `5` = 10L)
    )
}
```
